transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Ivy Chen (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Hummingbird CTO), Raj Mehta (ML Eng), Elena Park (Platform), Samir Khan (Dev)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): We ran a migration mapping demo focused on practical copy-paste steps: endpoint swap, param mapping (temperature/top_p), function-calls to Redwood structured output, streaming differences, embedding model names + dimensional parity, and batching/rate limit knobs in Console. Customer asked about Private/VPC, KMS, and cost comparisons.

[00:00:10] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin, I'm Sofia with Redwood. Marcus and Ivy will do the deep mapping. Dana, do you want to kick us off with where you are today?
[00:00:26] Dana: Yeah, thanks. we run most inference on OpenAI right now, a bit of Anthropic for chat, and TogetherAI for some internal models — mainly a mix of gpt-4x-ish from OpenAI and Claude for safetyy checks. goal is to reduce unit costs and get more control on private data.
[00:00:42] Raj: We have a microservice that hits openai.com/v1/chat/completions with a bunch of assistant messages, about 40 reqs/sec during peak. embedding calls are separate — we use ada-style for search vectors.
[00:00:55] Marcus: cool, that gives us the baseline. we'll demonstrate direct mappings, and then show where Redwood deviates and why (performance/cost tradeoffs).
[00:01:05] Ivy: also quick note — if you have any security constraints, flag them, we'll highlight Private and VPC options as we go.
[00:01:15] Elena: We do need KMS + audit logs, and likely SAML SSO. SOC2 is a yes.
[00:01:22] Sofia: good, we'll cover those. ok Marcus, take it away.

--- API parity & endpoint mapping ---
[00:01:35] Marcus: Alright, first slide — endpoint parity. OpenAI chat completions -> Redwood /v1/chat/generate equivalent. Together and Anthropic map to Redwood chat endpoints too, but there are small differences to watch: Anthropic has a different context tokenization and safety framing, Together sometimes uses different param names. The good news: request-level mapping is usually straightforward.
[00:02:02] Marcus: Key fields: messages -> messages, temperature -> temperature, top_p -> top_p, max_tokens -> max_tokens. For streaming, OpenAI uses chunked SSE. Redwood supports streaming with the same behavior but we use a slightly different payload framing when you opt in for structured outputs.
[00:02:26] Raj: Do we need to change client libs? we use openai-js right now.
[00:02:30] Marcus: short answer: no, but we recommend a small adapter layer. example: replace baseURL and update model name, and a 2-3 line shim for streaming events if you consume raw SSE. we will share code snippets.
[00:02:46] Ivy: I'll show a Console snippet in a sec that auto-generates SDK samples.

[00:02:55] Marcus: now function-calls — customers always trip here. OpenAI's functions model returns a 'function_call' object and Anthropic has a different signature. Redwood provides structured output and a function-calling compatibility shim. you can map OpenAI function schemas into Redwood's schema with the provided tool.
[00:03:18] Raj: Is there a 1:1 mapping for nested objects? some of our functions expect complex json blobs.
[00:03:22] Marcus: most nested schemas map fine; caveat: Anthropic sometimes flattens certain fields — you'll want to validate with the tools. Marcus: (laugh) we'll include a converter script for your nested payloads.

[00:03:38] [00:03:42] Dana: What about streaming plus function-calls? we rely on partial outputs for progressive UI.
[00:03:47] Marcus: Redwood supports streaming tokens plus an event that indicates a function call start/complete. there was a small difference in how partial function args are emitted — our SDK will buffer until the function is complete by default, but you can opt to stream partial JSON if you like.

--- Embeddings and vectors ---
[00:04:10] Marcus: embeddings: OpenAI model 'text-embedding-ada-002' -> Redwood has curated equivalents (we'll call them 'redwood-embed-1', etc). dimensionality is preserved for parity options but sometimes the numbers differ; we give a migration path: reindex pipeline, or runtime crosswalk if you want to avoid full reindex.
[00:04:33] Raj: Crosswalk? you mean runtime conversion of vectors?
[00:04:36] Marcus: yeah, a lightweight projection layer — results are not identical but can be tuned. for high-precision search we recommend re-embedding.
[00:04:45] Elena: that has cost implications.
[00:04:47] Sofia: exactly why we have Optimize suggestions — it will tell you when re-embed is worthwhile vs runtime projection.

--- Rate limits, batching, and Console demo ---
[00:05:00] Ivy: switching to Console — quick live demo. (typing noises) the Console has API keys, per-route throttles, and a batching profile manager. here I'm showing your current OpenAI-like traffic shape imported from a CSV — you can create a batching policy that groups small prompts into 128-token buckets to reduce unit cost.
[00:05:28] Ivy: note: the batching settings are workload-aware; we simulate cost impact before you apply.
[00:05:36] Raj: How do we balance latency SLOs? we need sub-250ms for short-completions.
[00:05:41] Marcus: you create routes: low-latency route bypasses batching with reserved capacity (Dedicated), cost-optimized route uses batching + cache. Smart routing can failover to hosted if dedicated is congested.
[00:05:55] Dana: Can we do per-customer routing? each tenant has different SLAs.
[00:06:00] Marcus: yes, per-api-key routing and token-level cost allocation.

--- Quantization and cost controls ---
[00:06:12] Marcus: on the runtime side, Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles and model variants. for example, a 4-bit quantized variant might trade 2-3% accuracy on your evals but cut token cost by 40%. We'll run your eval set and show delta.
[00:06:29] Raj: We need visibility into regressions.
[00:06:31] Marcus: built-in evals and drift alerts, tied to versions and prompt-sets. we also offer canary rollouts.

--- Security & Private Deployment ---
[00:06:45] Sofia: short security piece: VPC/private control plane available. KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logging across requests. Marcus, any caveats?
[00:06:58] Marcus: network topology matters for latency; on-prem will have extra hops vs hosted. we can provide a deployment checklist. there was a note about egress and private peering — that affects throughput testing.
[00:07:09] Elena: audit logs granularity? we need token-level request logs retained 90 days.
[00:07:14] Sofia: yes, we have configurable retention with exports to your SIEM.

--- Live mapping walkthrough (practical) ---
[00:07:30] Marcus: Ok, practical part. I'll paste a side-by-side example. (reads) OpenAI: POST /v1/chat/completions with model=gpt-4-x, messages, temperature. Redwood: POST /v1/chat/generate model=redwood-8x or redwood-avx, messages, temperature. change model names, tweak max_tokens -> response_limit, and you're 95% there.
[00:07:58] Marcus: for streaming: OpenAI SSE events with 'data: {delta}', Redwood SSE uses 'event: token' chunks with an optional 'structured' wrapper. small adapter code in Node: replace event parsing and map the 'token' to the same UI chunking.
[00:08:18] Raj: will the adapter be open source?
[00:08:20] Marcus: yes, we'll drop it in a repo.

[00:08:27] Marcus: now Anthropic: their 'completion' style includes system prompts and 'safety' signals. Redwood normalizes system -> messages[0] and attaches a safety meta header. Theres a small diff where Anthropic includes a 'deterministic' flag. We map deterministic -> temperature 0.
[00:08:47] Dana: TogetherAI — any gotchas?
[00:08:49] Marcus: Together sometimes uses different tokenization and model families; mapping is model-name swap plus validating prompt length. They also expose a different max sequence len; Redwood runtime will accept long context but you may want to trim.

[00:09:04] Ivy: I'm showing the Console 'Migrate' wizard — you can import configs from a JSON manifest (we accept OpenAI-style manifests) and it produces a paritity checklist and suggested changes. the wizard flags function-schemas, streaming consumers, and embedding dims.
[00:09:20] Raj: nice. how does pricing compare?
[00:09:24] Sofia: high-level: for hosted API the per-token unit price for comparable models is typically 10-30% lower; Dedicated is a committed compute model that makes sense if you have sustained throughput. We'll send a cost-per-1M-token example.

--- Performance & benchmarking ---
[00:09:40] Marcus: let's talk benchmark plan — we'll run a 1h window with your traffic replay (you provide sample request CSV). We'll test latency P50/P95 and token-cost. Also test embedding recall for the search set.
[00:09:56] Dana: do you support GPU types? we need A100-level perf for some workloads.
[00:10:01] Marcus: yes Dedicated supports A100 and H100 fleets; private on-prem can be tailored. we pick kernels and quantization based on model and seq length.

--- Customer questions and common pitfalls ---
[00:10:15] Samir: a practical question — our devs hard-coded OpenAI model names in 12 repos. what's the recommended migration path?
[00:10:22] Ivy: small adapter npm package, and a one-time codemod to replace baseURL + model mapping. we also provide CI checks to catch old model names.
[00:10:33] Raj: mental model for error handling? 429s, rate-limited requests.
[00:10:36] Marcus: Redwood returns standard HTTP 429 with a retry-after header; Console will surface per-key throttles and backpressure metrics. for Dedicated we can tune quota.

--- Demo: Optimize suggestions ---
[00:10:50] Ivy: showing Optimize tab — here we have a recommendation engine that looks at token distribution and suggests batch size, cache TTL, and quantization level. example: for your short chat completions we recommend small-batch, cache common prefixes, and a mid-tier quantized model. projected saving: ~38% with <2% eval delta.
[00:11:12] Dana: interesting. do you have a regression dashboard?
[00:11:15] Marcus: yes, evals show diffs per-prompt and you can roll back by version.

--- Cross-team concerns: compliance and procurement ---
[00:11:25] Elena: procurement will ask about data residency and contracts. we are EU-based clients.
[00:11:29] Sofia: Redwood has EU regions and Private deployments to satisfy residency. We'll include legal templates and SCCs in the pack.

--- Misrecognitions and small talk ---
[00:11:40] Raj: also... um sometimes we see tokenization mismatches with emoji and very short prompts.
[00:11:45] Marcus: yeah, those are common — tests in Optimize catch those.
[00:11:48] Dana: great. (laughs) thanks Marcus.

--- Recap and explicit next steps ---
[00:11:55] Sofia: quick recap — Marcus will share the parity spreadsheet and converter scripts; I will send pricing and the security pack; Raj will send the 1k prompt sample and traffic CSV; Elena to confirm VPC options. we'll schedule a 1h perf validation next week.
[00:12:14] Marcus: also hooking up a sandbox tenant for Hummingbird so you can run internal smoke tests.
[00:12:19] Dana: that all sounds good — thanks.

--- Closing notes (transcription resumes noise) ---
[00:12:30] Sofia: ok we'll wrap. thanks team.
[00:12:33] Raj: bye.
